deckTitle: MedKayfab Elemental Wrestling: The Atomic Arena

cards.power: Gradient Mastery. Creates or collapses pH balance.
cards.lore: Drives mitochondrial ATP, rising H+ crashes hemoglobin's oxygen affinity (Bohr Effect).
cards.gradeReason: Mechanism is solid but invites description over embodied performance at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Glowing proton sprite splitting water molecule. Mood: Electric and volatile.

cards.power: Structural Sovereignty. Multiglobing = structural disease.
cards.lore: Builds stable covalent backbones; replacing a single atom alters entire receptor affinities.
cards.gradeReason: Sovereignty is promising but Multiglobing needs table explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Octopus with carbon-chain tentacles gripping DNA helix. Mood: Structural and ancient.

cards.power: Vital Combustion. Sustains life via ATP; destroys via Oxidative Stress (ROS).
cards.lore: The final electron acceptor; sparks lethal reperfusion injury after ischemia.
cards.gradeReason: Dual-use concept is good but two-sided power needs context to play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Fiery butterfly half-angel half-burning wraith. Mood: Life-giving and deadly.

cards.power: Protein Synthesis. Builds the Muscles of the cell.
cards.lore: High Urea indicates waste failure; negative N-balance is an ICU casualty red flag.
cards.gradeReason: Muscle-builder framing is clear but the lore pivot to ICU flags is a mid-card gear shift.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Blue spider weaving protein strands across a cell. Mood: Industrious and clinical.

cards.power: Energy Transfer. Powers every cellular move.
cards.lore: The P in ATP. Refeeding Syndrome causes lethal serum drops.
cards.gradeReason: Powers every cellular move — you know exactly what this card does. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Electric eel coiled around ATP molecule sparking with energy. Mood: High-voltage and essential.

cards.power: Structural Stability. Holds the frame together.
cards.lore: Disulfide bridges lock Insulin and Keratin in place; breaking them denatures the unit.
cards.gradeReason: Solid mechanic but holds the frame together is holding-pattern language.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Armored welder bonding two protein chains with sulfur bridges. Mood: Industrial and stoic.

cards.power: Osmotic Balance & Killing. Balances Na+ and makes immune bleach.
cards.lore: Drives the RBC Chloride Shift; hyperchloremia triggers metabolic acidosis.
cards.gradeReason: Two jobs on one card dilutes the identity; which fight is this card in?
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Praying mantis spraying bleach through cell membranes. Mood: Toxic and utilitarian.

cards.power: Hardness Buff. Protects the dental arena.
cards.lore: Strengthens hydroxyapatite; excess causes mottled enamel (Fluorosis).
cards.gradeReason: Hardness Buff is playable but Fluorosis parenthetical reads like footnote, not move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Armadillo with crystalline enamel armor shielding giant molar. Mood: Defensive and mineral.

cards.power: Electrical Trigger. Fires neurons; high Na+ shrinks cells.
cards.lore: Drives action potentials; correcting too fast breaks the Mainframe Brain.
cards.gradeReason: Fires neurons — every player at the table knows exactly what this card is doing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Leopard launching lightning bolt down nerve fiber. Mood: Fast and electric.

cards.power: Electrical Reset. Hyperkalemia stalls the Cardiac Engine.
cards.lore: Defines resting membrane potential; Insulin therapy drives K+ out of the serum.
cards.gradeReason: Stalls the Cardiac Engine — you know the stakes and the move. Crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Sloth pressing pause button on glowing heartbeat monitor. Mood: Slow and dangerous.

cards.power: Signal Dampening. Calms the Bipolar Storm.
cards.lore: Mimics Na+ in the brain; toxicity causes fine tremor and renal crash if Na+ intake drops.
cards.gradeReason: Calms the Bipolar Storm is clinical shorthand perfection — emotionally and medically legible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Giant tortoise smoothing out wild EEG wave mountains. Mood: Steady and medicated.

cards.power: Tracer Vision. Follows the K-Path to reveal perfusion gaps.
cards.lore: K-mimic used in PET scans to track hidden blood flow in the Heart Engine.
cards.gradeReason: Niche tracer role is interesting but PET scan context is specialist knowledge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Glowing spirit monkey following potassium channels through cardiac map. Mood: Spectral and diagnostic.

cards.power: Relaxation & Stability. Low Mag triggers Torsades-the-Twist.
cards.lore: Powers 300+ enzymes; acts as natural antidote for Eclampsia seiz[ures].
cards.gradeReason: Torsades-the-Twist is an instant mnemonic — the name alone earns G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Bull holding giant magnet attracting enzyme cofactors. Mood: Powerful and stabilizing.

cards.power: Signal-to-Action. Low Ca causes The Tetany-Twitch.
cards.lore: Universal second messenger driving contraction, neurotransmitters, and coagulation.
cards.gradeReason: Tetany-Twitch is embodied — you know the move and the cost of missing it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Kangaroo kicking muscle fibers with calcium sparks exploding. Mood: Urgent and kinetic.

cards.power: Matrix-Reinforcement. Increases bone density but confuses Calcium.
cards.lore: Behaves like Calcium; radioactive Sr-90 is lethally toxic to the Marrow-Factory.
cards.gradeReason: Interesting impostor mechanic but confuses Calcium is description not performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Rhino in calcium disguise infiltrating bone matrix. Mood: Deceptive and radioactive.

cards.power: The Opaque-Painter. Coats the GI-Tunnel to reveal ulcers.
cards.lore: Toxic if absorbed; safe as an insoluble sulfate Chalky-Drink to block X-rays.
cards.gradeReason: The Opaque-Painter is a cinematic image — you see the move before you finish reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: White elephant painting intestinal walls with barium brush, x-ray glow behind. Mood: Diagnostic and luminous.

cards.power: Gas Transport. Fuels the arena; Anemia = System Hypoxia.
cards.lore: The heart of Hemoglobin; Heme vs. Non-Heme absorption dictates bio-availability.
cards.gradeReason: Reliable framing but Gas Transport is workhorse language, not a wrestling headline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Beetle carrying oxygen spheres in glowing red hemoglobin armor. Mood: Essential and relentless.

cards.power: Energy Linkage. Bridges Iron and Oxygen; high Cu = Wilson's disease.
cards.lore: Powers Cytochrome C; toxicity leaves Kayser-Fleischer rings in the Eye-Arena.
cards.gradeReason: Kayser-Fleischer rings in the Eye-Arena is great lore but the power name is flat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Fox with copper-green eyes operating electron transport chain. Mood: Precise and toxic.

cards.power: Gene Expression. Zinc-Fingers hack the DNA code.
cards.lore: Runs 2000+ transcription factors; deficiency causes Acrodermatitis and taste loss.
cards.gradeReason: Zinc-Fingers hack the DNA code — hacker framing makes this instantly performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Raccoon with zinc claw-fingers cracking open DNA helix. Mood: Precise and transgressive.

cards.power: Antioxidant Shield. Defends against ROS Oxyra-Fragments.
cards.lore: Superoxide dismutase co-factor; toxicity closely mirrors Parkinson-the-Tremor.
cards.gradeReason: Shield role is clear but Oxyra-Fragments requires cross-card knowledge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Armored pangolin deflecting free radical shards with scaly shield. Mood: Defensive and chemical.

cards.power: Nerve Protection. Missing Cobo melts the Myelin-Sleeve.
cards.lore: Central atom of B12; deficiency causes Megaloblastic (Macro-filia) anemia and stumbles.
cards.gradeReason: Melts the Myelin-Sleeve is viscerally specific — the consequence is the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Blue hermit crab inside B12 shell protecting nerve fibers from dissolving. Mood: Protective and fragile.

cards.power: The Contact-Riot. Master of triggering Type IV hypersensitivity.
cards.lore: Not biologically required; the undisputed champion of Jewelry-Dermatitis.
cards.gradeReason: Contact-Riot lands but Type IV hypersensitivity stops non-immunologists cold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Spiky porcupine leaving red rash on skin everywhere it touches. Mood: Irritating and allergic.

cards.power: Waste Processing. Clears DNA debris; excess causes Gouty-George-Grit.
cards.lore: Essential for Xanthine oxidase to process purine Waste-Code into Uric Acid.
cards.gradeReason: Gouty-George-Grit is fun naming but the function is janitorial, not heroic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Vulture dissolving purine waste crystals with enzyme beak. Mood: Industrial and unglamorous.

cards.power: Glucose Potentiator. Enhances Insu-the-Key for cell entry.
cards.lore: Regulates the Sugar-Stat; beware the hexavalent form—it is a Mutagenic-Vandal.
cards.gradeReason: Mutagenic-Vandal is great flavor but the power name Glucose Potentiator is flat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Chameleon morphing between insulin key and carcinogenic toxin. Mood: Dual-natured and metallic.

cards.power: Metabolic Throttle. Controls the Speed-of-the-Match.
cards.lore: Builds T3/T4; deficiency stalls the thyroid and swells the neck (Hypo-Hanna-Goiter).
cards.gradeReason: Metabolic Throttle + Speed-of-the-Match — wrestling framing lands exactly right.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Purple toad clutching thyroid throttle dial, neck pulsing with energy. Mood: Regulatory and vital.

cards.power: Systemic Dampening. Calms nerves but triggers Bromism delirium.
cards.lore: Competes with Chlorine; phased out as a sedative for safer Benzo Mind-Mules.
cards.gradeReason: Obsolete-sedative story is interesting but Systemic Dampening is too vague.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Skunk spraying sedative cloud over nervous system with sleep-z symbols. Mood: Dampening and historical.

cards.power: Easy Flow. Reduces the Work-of-Breathing.
cards.lore: Low density turns turbulent storms into laminar breezes to bypass Airway-Clogs.
cards.gradeReason: Clinical role is legible but Easy Flow is too soft a name for a wrestling move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Hummingbird gliding through turbulent airway tunnel, smoothing eddies. Mood: Effortless and clinical.

cards.power: The Perfect-Sleep. Neuroprotective NMDA-antagonist anesthetic.
cards.lore: Induces a Heart-Halt state without the Heart-Halt side effects for high-risk ICU wrestlers.
cards.gradeReason: The Perfect-Sleep is great; NMDA-antagonist mid-power kills the momentum.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: White owl inducing glowing sleep state in ICU heart still beating. Mood: Serene and neuroprotective.

cards.power: Radical Neutralization. Disarms ROS before they rip the cell membrane.
cards.lore: Heart of Glutathione Peroxidase; deficiency causes Keshan Disease cardiomyopathy.
cards.gradeReason: Before they rip the cell membrane is vivid but Radical Neutralization is generic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Pelican catching free radical bullets mid-air with selenocysteine net. Mood: Protective and scarce.

cards.power: Structural Integrity. Excess (inhaled) causes Silico-the-Lung-Grinder.
cards.lore: Crucial for collagen crosslinking; inhaling it grinds the lungs into fibrosis.
cards.gradeReason: Lung-Grinder is visceral but the dual role in structure vs. toxicity splits focus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Crystal butterfly with industrial dust cloud grinding lungs into stone. Mood: Beautiful and hazardous.

cards.power: The Metabolic Mimic. Yields zero energy, starving the cell in a sea of fuel.
cards.lore: Sabotages ATP and Pyruvate Dehydrogenase; causes garlic breath and Mees-lines.
cards.gradeReason: Starving the cell in a sea of fuel is brilliant lore but The Metabolic Mimic is cold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Rat disguised as ATP molecule draining energy from mitochondria. Mood: Deceptive and poisonous.

cards.power: Mineral Regulation. Keeps the Bone-Stat steady.
cards.lore: Regulates Calcium and Magnesium; key player in post-menopausal bone health quests.
cards.gradeReason: Keeps the Bone-Stat steady is a nursing note, not a fight call. Weakest card in deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Woodpecker tapping bone mineral balance scale between calcium and magnesium. Mood: Understated and supportive.

cards.power: The Mainframe-Corrosive. Shatters Enzyme-Gears.
cards.lore: Binds sulfhydryl groups; organic methyl-mercury triggers Mad-Hatter tremors.
cards.gradeReason: Shatters Enzyme-Gears — pure destructive action, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Liquid silver serpent dissolving enzyme machinery in toxic splash. Mood: Corrosive and neurological.

cards.power: The Anemia-Artist. Stops iron from entering the Hemoglobin-Ring.
cards.lore: Inhibits Ferrochelatase; causes basophilic stippling, lead lines on gums, and wrist drop.
cards.gradeReason: The Anemia-Artist is the name AND the diagnosis. Clinically perfect G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Grey elephant sitting on hemoglobin ring blocking iron entry, stippled brushwork. Mood: Heavy and toxic.

cards.power: The Filter-Destroyer. Accumulates in Renal-Tubes.
cards.lore: Mimics Zinc; leaches bone minerals causing Ita-Ita (Ouch-Ouch) bone pain. High risk for smokers.
cards.gradeReason: Filter-Destroyer is strong but Accumulates in Renal-Tubes describes rather than strikes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Green toad crushing renal tubule while stealing zinc badge off bone cells. Mood: Slow and accumulating.

cards.power: The Microbial-Burn. Destroys bacterial cell walls on contact.
cards.lore: Toxic to prokaryotes; excess in humans deposits permanently in skin under sunlight (Argyria).
cards.gradeReason: Destroys bacterial cell walls on contact — immediate, physical, unmistakable action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Silver chameleon emitting antimicrobial light dissolving bacteria on contact. Mood: Gleaming and lethal.

cards.power: The Rebellion-Stopper. Cross-links DNA (Cisplatin) to stop division.
cards.lore: High-power Chemo-Artillery fighting cancer; beware deafness and kidney-failure side effects.
cards.gradeReason: The Rebellion-Stopper is exactly what Cisplatin does — clinically accurate and visceral.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Silver crocodile clamping DNA strands shut, cancer cells frozen. Mood: Aggressive and clinical.

cards.power: The Immune-Mute. Calms the Joint-Riot.
cards.lore: Chrysotherapy inhibits macrophages; mostly replaced today by modern Biologic Brawlers.
cards.gradeReason: Calms the Joint-Riot — four words you can physically perform at a rheumatology table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Golden retriever silencing inflamed joint macrophages with warm paw. Mood: Noble and anti-inflammatory.

cards.power: The Insulin-Proxy. Activates the insulin receptor without insulin.
cards.lore: An insulin-mimetic investigated for Diabetes-Quests; but limited by heavy metal toxicity.
cards.gradeReason: Fascinating mechanism but experimental status makes this feel unfinished.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Blue lizard wearing insulin disguise unlocking glucose door on cell. Mood: Experimental and cautious.

cards.power: The Surface-Seal. Blocks Acid-Assassins from the tooth-pulp.
cards.lore: Used as Stannous Fluoride; outperforms Sodium Fluoride for Gingivitis-Defense.
cards.gradeReason: Acid-Assassins blocked at the tooth-pulp — defensive image is immediate and dental.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Tin beaver sealing tooth enamel gate against acid invaders. Mood: Defensive and dental.

cards.power: The Signal-Booster. Highlights Blood-Brain Barrier leaks.
cards.lore: Must be chelated to prevent toxicity; deadly NSF risk in Nephro-Ray-Failure patients.
cards.gradeReason: Highlights Blood-Brain Barrier leaks — cinematic, diagnostic, immediately actionable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Deep-sea anglerfish illuminating brain lesion in glowing MRI tunnel. Mood: Revealing and paramagnetic.

cards.power: The Meta-Radar. Attaches to supply trains for SPECT-Imaging.
cards.lore: Short 6-hour half-life; the undisputed Gold-Standard for Bone-Scan quests.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-Radar is fun but SPECT-Imaging requires nuclear medicine context to play.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Bat attaching to bone-supply train emitting gamma radiation signals. Mood: Radioactive and time-limited.

cards.power: The K-Infiltrator. Mimics Potassium to enter the heart, then halts it.
cards.lore: Lethal poison causing extreme neuropathy and massive hair loss (Hair-Loss-Hall).
cards.gradeReason: Enters the heart, then halts it — the most dramatic single move in the deck. Perfect G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Sloth in potassium disguise entering cardiac gate then freezing it solid. Mood: Treacherous and lethal.

cards.power: The Nephro-Smasher. Chemically toxic long before radiation hits.
cards.lore: Depleted Uranium is primarily a chemical threat that obliterates the proximal tubules.
cards.gradeReason: Nephro-Smasher lands hard — and the subversion of radiation fear is brilliant design.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Glowing green hippo smashing renal tubules with chemical fist. Mood: Heavy-metal toxic and radioactive.

cards.power: The Metal-Allergy. Dust triggers a Chronic-Immune-Riot.
cards.lore: Mimics Magnesium but causes system lag; Berylliosis mimics Sarcoid-the-Scar on X-rays.
cards.gradeReason: Chronic-Immune-Riot is good but The Metal-Allergy names the category not the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Polar bear releasing lung-scarring dust cloud, immune cells rioting. Mood: Industrial and chronic.

cards.power: The Bone-Bonder. The immune system ignores it.
cards.lore: Highly bio-inert; the champion material for joint replacements and Osseointegration.
cards.gradeReason: The immune system ignores it — four words that tell you everything. Irreducibly perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Giant tortoise with titanium shell fusing silently into bone, immune cells walking past. Mood: Inert and permanent.

cards.power: The Energy-Starver. Cuts off glycolysis fuel to the Micro-Punks.
cards.lore: First-line move (Sodium Stibogluconate) against Leishmaniasis (Leish-the-Skin-Eater).
cards.gradeReason: Cutting off glycolysis fuel to Micro-Punks is a wrestling metaphor that plays itself.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Heron strangling parasite fuel line mid-glycolysis, Leishmania withering. Mood: Targeted and antiparasitic.

cards.power: The Rhythm-Hacker. Mimics Potassium but causes massive QT-Interval-Stretch.
cards.lore: Ingestion leads to Torsades-de-Pointes; Cs-137 is a long-term fallout vandal.
cards.gradeReason: Rhythm-Hacker is a strong identity but QT-Interval-Stretch stops non-cardiologists.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Watercolor creature. Subject: Glowing cesium-blue cat hacking cardiac rhythm on ECG monitor. Mood: Radioactive and dysrhythmic.

cards.power: The Trace-Revealer. Finds a single lead speck in a blood pool.
cards.lore: Uses light to see the specific Atomic-Signatures of elements.
cards.gradeReason: Concept card — legible but functions as a tool, not a fighter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steampunk watercolor. Subject: Owl with spectroscope eyes reading atomic signatures in blood sample. Mood: Precise and forensic.

cards.power: The Metal-Grabber. Cages toxic Trace-Titans and drains them out.
cards.lore: Prevents rebound metals from vandalizing enzymes during Chelation Therapy.
cards.gradeReason: Cages toxic Trace-Titans and drains them out — a healer with a visual signature.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steampunk watercolor. Subject: Birdcage trapping glowing heavy-metal creatures, dragging them toward kidney drain. Mood: Clinical and resolving.

cards.power: The Acid-Meter. pH 7.4 is the Equilibrium-Zone.
cards.lore: It is logarithmic; a tiny number shift means a massive change in Protonis power.
cards.gradeReason: Good teacher card but Equilibrium-Zone is a location, not a move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steampunk watercolor. Subject: Lemur balancing pH scale with fire on acid side and ice water on base side. Mood: Precise and volatile.

cards.power: The Electron-Thief-Score. Predicts who steals the charge.
cards.lore: High score dictates the ultimate thief; fundamentally dictates Ionic vs. Covalent bonding.
cards.gradeReason: Electron-Thief framing is smart but Predicts is passive — not a performer yet.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steampunk watercolor. Subject: Angel figure with electron-stealing wings scoring bonds on Pauling scale chart. Mood: Abstract and fundamental.

cards.power: The Atomic-Balancer.
cards.lore: Master the elements or the wrestling ring collapses into dust! Are the protons flowing? Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Host card with full kayfabe authority — every player knows exactly who runs this ring.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cartoon watercolor. Subject: Rabbit in lab coat holding up both elements and wrestling belt. Mood: Manic and authoritative.

cards.power: The Chloride Shift.
cards.lore: When Proton Army levels skyrocket, the Acid-Base-Sherif (Chlorine) must balance the shift.
cards.gradeReason: Scenario is legible but The Chloride Shift needs Chlorax context to fully activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Action watercolor. Subject: Axolotl and mantis in pH acid-base tug of war, CO2 bubbles rising. Mood: Urgent and chemical.

cards.power: Clearing the Rust.
cards.lore: Bronze skin + failing liver = Oxygen-Bearer gone rogue; requires Chelator-the-Cage to fix.
cards.gradeReason: The Rusting Liver is a clinical picture in three words — diagnosis and scenario in one.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Action watercolor. Subject: Iron-overloaded liver rusting bronze while chelator cage descends to trap excess iron. Mood: Urgent and corrective.

cards.power: Rate-Stabilizer.
cards.lore: K-rich diets + Kidney stalls = Lethal Reset-Current; Calcium is the shield to protect the heart-wires.
cards.gradeReason: Spark-Failure is a vivid scenario name but Rate-Stabilizer as a power is generic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Action watercolor. Subject: Otter and sloth ECG battle, peaked T-wave mountains, calcium shield blocking. Mood: Cardiac and emergency.

verdict: Fifty-six elements suited up for the Atomic Arena, each packing a clinical Power and lore that earns its ring space. The naming system is letter-perfect: Thallo the K-Infiltrator enters the heart then halts it, Lithos Calms the Bipolar Storm, Titan gets a bye because the immune system simply ignores it. One genuine weak link: Boros (Boron) brings a nursing note where it should bring a fight call. As a MedKayfab entry point for biochemistry and elemental toxicology, this is the strongest deck in the series to date. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: For med students and science nerds who want the periodic table to actually stick — 56 elements reimagined as clinical wrestlers, each with a move that could save a life on rounds.

coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — MEDKAYFAB ELEMENTAL WRESTLING / THE ATOMIC ARENA is punchy, clear, and stacks the two brand names correctly
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — periodic table as wrestling arena is the exact premise; cover delivers the promise without confusion

coverQA.coverNote: Cleanest MedKayfab cover to date — the dual element spheres (H glowing blue, C in dark matter black) flanking FrizzleBob creates instant drama. The Master the Table, Master the Life-Code. Stay Fluffy! tagline is exactly the right register. Minor: text density in the subtitle block is high for small-print viewing.

notes: 15-page deck. Pages 2-13 contain elemental character cards (4 per page, 48 cards). Page 14 has concept/mechanic cards: AAS spectroscopy, Chelation, pH scale, Electronegativity (4 cards). Page 15 has Doc FrizzleBob host card + 3 Synthesis Quest scenario cards. All artwork is consistent high-quality watercolor style with distinctive animal/creature representations per element. KayfaBINGO!, Diagnosis?!, KayfaBOGGLE! watermarks appear on several pages as decorative overlays — consistent with other MedKayfab decks. STAT line format is consistent: Element Type | Period/Group | Key Property. Some LORE text is very small at print scale — not a digital readability issue. RAF dice boxes absent from page 14 mechanic cards.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: THE ATOMIC ARENA – The Periodic Table That Heals and Kills (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the trace metals your enzymes cannot run without, the heavy metals that poison those same enzymes, and the electrolytes that decide whether a heart keeps its rhythm.

You learned the periodic table once, for one exam, and filed it under chemistry you would never need again. Your patients never filed it anywhere. It is running in their cells right now, and the gap between a cofactor and a poison is often nothing more than the dose and which protein the atom grabbed on the way in. Lead draws a blue line on the gums and drops the wrist. Magnesium is the thing you push to stop an eclamptic seizure that nothing else will touch. A small shift in potassium can stop a heart that was beating fine a minute ago.

MedKayfab: The Atomic Arena turns the medical half of the periodic table into a narrative wrestling match. Every element walks into the ring as a character with a day job and a body count. Stop reciting atomic numbers. Start learning which element is keeping the patient alive and which one is quietly taking them apart.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like Zinco, Plumbos, and Mag-the-Magnet
- Free lifetime updates as the science is refined
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the chemistry the body actually runs on, the good faces and the assassins side by side. You'll meet Zinco, who quietly runs over two thousand transcription factors and, the moment he walks out, answers with acrodermatitis and a lost sense of taste. You'll meet Plumbos, lead in a wrestling singlet, who jams the enzyme ferrochelatase, stipples the red cells, and signs his work with a line on the gums and a dropped wrist. And you'll meet Mag-the-Magnet, who powers more than three hundred enzymes on a normal day and becomes the antidote you reach for when an eclamptic seizure has to end now. The heavy-metal roster, Mercurio and Arseno among them, rounds out the villain side of the card.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for high-stress retrieval. You have the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the numbers and thresholds), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is the test that matters: name what the element does to the enzyme, and what it does to the patient, in one sentence without looking, or the "patient" on the Stage doesn't make it.

Honest cognitive load
This is a B-tier novelty engine, not a ward-day survival deck. Its immediate clinical utility is narrow on purpose; its real job is to make the chemistry finally connect to a living body so the wards make sense later. It sits one rung below Biochemistry on the learning staircase, which is exactly why it pairs so well with the Biochemistry deck as a foundation, while the heavy-metal toxicology roster hands off cleanly to Essential Pharmacology. Best for preclinical students who never forgave the periodic table, and for anyone who wants the trace elements and electrolytes to stop being a list.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free.
If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. If you're a student on a budget, enter €0. No questions asked. If you want to support more decks, anything above fair price is appreciated.
CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
